title: Air India Deepens Salesforce AI Bet to Speed Up Customer Service
excerpt: Air India is expanding its deployment of Salesforce's Agentforce agentic AI across customer service, automating complex email requests, cutting name corrections from days to 30 minutes, and giving agents a conversational knowledge assistant.
body:
• Air India has expanded its deployment of Salesforce's Agentforce agentic AI platform across customer service operations, building on its April 2025 go-live with automated refund handling.
  • Specialised AI sub-agents now parse multi-request customer emails covering refunds, baggage and loyalty, validating information across systems and consolidating answers into a single response.
  • Name corrections that once took about three days now take 30 minutes; a new Knowledge Agent gives service staff conversational access to fare rules, policies and operational guidance.
  • The expansion is part of a broader programme of more than 30 agentic AI initiatives running across Air India's cloud-first ecosystem of 140-plus enterprise systems.

Air India has expanded its use of Salesforce's Agentforce platform to automate a broader set of customer service workflows, marking the latest step in the Tata Group-owned carrier's push to become what it calls an AI-first airline.

The expansion builds on the airline's April 2025 rollout, when Air India became one of the first airlines in the world to go live with Agentforce, initially to speed up the handling of refund requests. The company said the latest deployments move its agentic AI from assisting employees toward executing complex workflows on its own, within defined guardrails and with human oversight where required.

Automating complex requests

A central feature of the expansion is automated email resolution. Agentforce can now identify multiple requests inside a single customer email — spanning refunds, baggage and loyalty — and deploy specialised sub-agents to gather and validate information, execute the required actions and consolidate the outcome into a single reply built on Air India-approved templates. For eligible cases, responses are generated only when the system exceeds a 95 per cent confidence threshold, with human intervention where necessary.

Name corrections, a process involving multiple eligibility checks, validations and ticketing actions, have also been brought under the AI workflow. The airline said Agentforce coordinates these steps, including initiating ticket reissuance and delivering the updated ticket to the customer, cutting turnaround time from approximately three days to 30 minutes.

Air India has additionally deployed a Knowledge Agent for its customer service representatives. The conversational AI assistant provides real-time access to policies, procedures, fare rules and operational guidance, reducing the need to search across multiple knowledge repositories during live interactions. The company reported improvements in response consistency, agent onboarding and first-contact resolution rates.

“Our journey with Agentforce is not simply about deploying AI; it is about redefining what is possible in airline customer service. We are moving from AI that assists our teams to AI that can understand, decide and execute within clearly defined guardrails.” — Dr. Satya Ramaswamy, Chief Digital & Technology Officer, Air India

Context & Background

Air India has been a long-standing Salesforce customer, using Service Cloud, Sales Cloud, Data Cloud and Einstein AI to power customer engagement and business operations. The carrier has been consolidating customer data from its call centre systems, passenger service systems and enterprise data lakes into a unified profile through Salesforce Data Cloud, giving service representatives a complete view of each customer during interactions. The airline handles about 550,000 service cases a month through Salesforce Service Cloud.

The AI push sits inside the airline's wider Vihaan.AI digital transformation plan, under which Air India has built a cloud-first ecosystem spanning more than 140 enterprise systems. The company evaluates its agentic AI work across four areas: increasing revenue, reducing cost, improving customer experience, and enabling capabilities that were previously not possible.

Impact & Analysis

The shift matters because refunds, name corrections and baggage disputes are among the highest-friction interactions in airline customer service, often requiring multiple handoffs between the contact centre, specialist teams and the customer. Automating the routine steps — while holding AI-generated customer-facing responses to a 95 per cent confidence threshold with human fallback — addresses the two risks airlines fear most in automation: wrong answers delivered at scale and customers trapped in bot loops.

Arundhati Bhattacharya, President and CEO of Salesforce South Asia, said the partnership shows customer experience being defined “not simply by how quickly organisations respond, but by how intelligently they can act on behalf of customers.” For Salesforce, the deployment is a flagship reference in aviation, a sector where AI agents must operate against dense, rule-bound systems such as fare rules and ticketing workflows.

Diaspora Angle

Indian diaspora flyers are among Air India's heaviest users on long-haul international routes connecting the US, UK, Canada and the Gulf to India — precisely the journeys where booking complexities, name mismatches on passports and tickets, and refund disputes after schedule changes are most common. If the 30-minute name correction and automated email resolution perform as claimed, they would remove two of the most frequent service pain points for overseas Indian travellers, who often manage family bookings across time zones.

What's Next

Air India said it plans to scale Agentforce across other contact centre operations and customer touchpoints, including voice-based interactions, over the coming months. The real test will be whether the AI handles disruption-heavy periods — flight cancellations, schedule changes, baggage backlogs — without degrading accuracy, and whether the promised human oversight holds up when volumes spike. For now, the airline's measured claims focus on faster resolutions, lower customer effort and consistent responses rather than replacing agents, positioning AI as an execution layer under human governance.
